posts.title: The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate
posts.summary:
Is it better to cram more compute into each rack or rethink the architecture?
The post The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Hyperscalers including Google, Meta, and Microsoft are collaborating via the OCP 'Mount Diablo' project to standardize 1-megawatt rack architectures.
The transition to 1-megawatt racks necessitates a fundamental shift where the rack is treated as an integrated compute system rather than a passive enclosure.
Key technical hurdles for these high-density racks include advanced liquid cooling, high-voltage DC power delivery, and managing the massive increase in electrical signaling connections.
Industry experts are debating whether extreme rack density is a necessary evolution for AI workloads or if distributed, fragmented architectures might offer a more efficient alternative.

posts.title: Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip
posts.summary:
As AI clusters push beyond rack-scale limits, optical interconnects and circuit switching are reshaping how data centers scale. 
The post Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Copper interconnects are reaching physical limits regarding signal loss and power consumption, forcing a shift toward optical interconnects even within single racks.
Inefficient GPU utilization, often dropping to 25% due to data-wait times, is driving the industry to prioritize lower-latency optical circuit switching (OCS) networks.

The industry is adopting new terminology like 'scale-in' to describe the massive bandwidth requirements staying within a single chassis, reflecting the blurring lines between traditional scale-up and scale-out definitions.
Major players like Google are already implementing torus-configured optical networks to overcome the distance and bandwidth constraints inherent in copper-based scaling.

posts.title: What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale?
posts.summary:
The path to widespread deployment of co-packaged optics depends on solving challenges in manufacturing, testing, and operations.
The post What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Co-packaged optics (CPO) are transitioning from prototypes to production, initially targeting scale-out switch ASICs where copper bandwidth is insufficient.
Widespread adoption of CPO for scale-up networks—where thousands of XPUs must function as a single unit—remains the next major technical and commercial hurdle.
Success for CPO depends on maturing the entire ecosystem, specifically addressing manufacturing, testing, and supply chain reliability for high-volume deployment.
Industry leaders are focused on leveraging wavelength multiplication and higher modulation rates to ensure CPO provides the multi-generational scaling required for future AI infrastructure.

posts.title: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
posts.summary: The police-tech giant Flock is announcing today that it will change officers’ access to its nationwide network of license plate readers, in an apparent effort to quell a growing backlash and win back contracts lost amid concerns about mass surveillance and police abuse. Several changes aim directly at a problem that has made recent headlines:…
bullets: Flock is mandating that officers input a criminal case number for every search, a response to a Washington Post investigation identifying 46 instances of police using the 120,000-camera network for unauthorized stalking.
The company is making its automatic auditing system mandatory to flag suspicious search patterns, though the tool's efficacy remains unverified by independent third parties.
To mitigate privacy concerns, Flock now recommends that agencies reduce data retention periods from 30 days to seven days, though local departments retain the authority to override this setting.

Despite these new guardrails, critics argue that the system remains vulnerable to abuse because Flock does not verify the validity of entered case numbers, allowing officers to bypass safeguards with generic or nonsensical inputs.

posts.title: BYD's flash charging Qin Max sedan goes on sale in China for under $15,000
posts.summary:
The BYD Qin Max is the flagship of the Qin family, available in EV and DM-i versions.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD has launched the Qin Max sedan with a starting price of 99,900 yuan ($14,720), positioning it as a flagship model to revitalize the declining sales of its core Qin lineup.
The EV variant features second-generation Blade Battery technology, enabling ultra-fast charging that reaches 97% capacity in just nine minutes.
The DM-i plug-in hybrid version achieves a class-leading fuel consumption rate of 2.59 liters per 100 km and offers a combined range of 2,370 km.
The vehicle integrates advanced driver-assistance systems via the 'God's Eye B' LiDAR platform and includes a built-in AI agent to enhance competitiveness in the youth-oriented B-segment market.
